title: Frontend misclassifies test-module  as facade re-export (REQ-V7 facade-leak FP)
description:
During ecosystem dogfood (vampiro-tmf.2), the Rust frontend produces REQ-V7 facade-leak findings for private functions re-exported only by sibling test modules via `use super::*;`.

Example from dont: `parse_line_span` (private fn, L1) at main.rs:2359 is flagged as a facade-leak with `facade_scope: parse_line_span_tests` — the test module `mod parse_line_span_tests { use super::*; ... }` is treated as a public L4 facade re-export. Same for `source_key` at rules/mod.rs:248 (`facade_scope: source_key_tests`).

Test modules are not public facades; their `use super::*` brings private items into test scope only.

Fix: the frontend should not emit a FacadeReexport for modules whose name matches a test pattern (`*_tests`/`*_test`) or that are gated by `#[cfg(test)]` / not `pub`.

title: Carry per-slot argument binding on CIR edges for composition analysis
description: The composition tracer (0vb.4.2) operates over frontend call edges (source=caller, target=callee), which approximate the EARS data-flow edge. Add an optional argument-slot field to CirEdge (or a companion data-flow edge type) so the composition tracer compares the callee's codomain against the specific caller parameter slot that consumes it. Removes spurious findings on multi-param callers and enables precise parse_amount→apply_discount seam detection.

title: Julia frontend: duplicate node IDs for anonymous functions
description:
When multiple anonymous functions exist in the same file, the Julia frontend generates node IDs like 'jl:.../file.jl:<anonymous>' without disambiguation, causing duplicate node IDs.

Discovered by cross_language_stress_tests:
  - cross_language_julia_web_server: multiple '<anonymous>' collisions
  - cross_language_julia_data_analysis: same issue

Fix: include the line number or a counter in the stable ID for anonymous functions.

title: Python frontend: edges reference non-existent nodes for builtins like getattr
description:
The Python frontend creates edges to builtin functions (e.g. getattr) that are not extracted as graph nodes. This produces invalid edges whose targets don't exist.

Fix: filter out edges to builtin/non-extractable symbols, or extract them as graph nodes with a 'builtin' flag.

Discovered by cross_language_stress_tests (data_pipeline.py: getattr).

title: Clojure frontend: edges reference non-existent nodes for macros and constructors
description:
The Clojure frontend creates edges to nodes that were not extracted (macro calls, constructor calls). The following symbols appear as edge targets but have no corresponding node:
  - 'when-not' (macro, in data_processing.clj)
  - 'go-loop' (macro, in async_example.clj)
  - '->Response' (record constructor, in http_server.clj)

Fix: either extract these as graph nodes, or suppress edges to non-extractable symbols.

Discovered by cross_language_stress_tests.

title: Python frontend: duplicate node IDs for __init__ across classes
description:
When multiple classes in the same file define __init__, the Python frontend generates node IDs like 'py:.../cli.py:__init__' without class disambiguation, causing duplicate node IDs.

Discovered by cross_language_stress_tests:
  - cross_language_python_cli: Command.__init__ and Group.__init__ collide
  - cross_language_python_http_lib: Session.__init__ and HTTPErrorV.__init__ collide

Fix: include class name in the node stable ID, e.g. 'py:.../cli.py:Command.__init__' vs 'py:.../cli.py:Group.__init__'.
